title: Giving Feedback to a Team Member
paragraphs: As a team leader, Yasmin needs to give a junior colleague feedback about repeated small errors in his reports, something she has been putting off for two weeks out of discomfort.
She prepares carefully beforehand, deciding to focus on specific examples rather than vague criticism, and to acknowledge his genuine strengths before addressing the pattern of mistakes.
During the conversation, her colleague initially looks nervous, but relaxes once he realizes the feedback is specific and constructive rather than a general complaint about his overall performance.
A week later, his reports show noticeable improvement, and he thanks Yasmin directly for being clear instead of simply staying silent and letting the small errors continue unaddressed.
